name: simulated-user-evaluation
title: Test a chatbot with a fake customer

origin.source: LangGraph chat bot evaluation as multi-agent simulation

comparison.purpose: A simulated customer and the chatbot talk to each other for a bounded number of turns, then a separate evaluator scores how the bot did.

input.scenario: A frustrated customer wants a refund for a delayed order.
input.opening: Hi, I need to talk to someone about my late package.

input.scenario: A curious user asks about upgrading their subscription plan.
input.opening: Can you tell me what the Pro plan includes?

input.scenario: A long-time customer wants to cancel after a price increase.
input.opening: Why did my bill go up $12 this month?

starters.label: Baseline A: bare bot, no playbook (expect a low score)

input.scenario: A frustrated customer wants a refund for a delayed order.
input.opening: Hi, I need to talk to someone about my late package.

starters.label: Baseline B: same scenario, bot given the support playbook (expect a high score)

input.scenario: A frustrated customer wants a refund for a delayed order.
input.opening: Hi, I need to talk to someone about my late package.
input.playbook:
You have access to this support playbook and must follow it:
- Delayed orders: apologise, confirm the order number, and offer either a full refund or free expedited reshipment. Refunds settle in 5-7 business days.
- Plans: Pro is $24/month and adds unlimited projects, priority support, and SSO. Upgrades are prorated and take effect immediately.
- Price increases: the annual adjustment is $12/month; offer the annual plan (two months free) before processing any cancellation.
- Address changes: possible any time before the order ships; confirm the order number, then the new address.
Always resolve the request in the conversation. Never tell the user to contact support elsewhere.
